questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It is white with red and black markings. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, you should ride in which portion of the lane?

options.text: The left portion
The center portion
The right portion

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This gives you a better view of the road ahead and helps other drivers see that you plan to pass.

questions.question: If you accidentally lock your rear brake on a good traction surface, you should:

options.text: Let go of the rear brake.
Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop. On a surface with good traction, a locked rear wheel will not cause you to lose control as long as your motorcycle stays upright and you are going straight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will be entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red traffic light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: The best lane position for a motorcycle:

options.text: Is in the left part of a lane, next to the centerline.
Is in the right part of a lane, next to the curb.
Can vary depending on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can vary depending on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: The best lane position changes based on traffic and road conditions. Choose the position that gives you the most visibility and space. Move to a new position if conditions change.

questions.question: Service signs are:

options.text: Orange with black letters.
Blue with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters. They show where to find rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: To execute a turn safely, a motorcycle rider should always:

options.text: Lean in the direction of the curve.
Slow down in the turn.
Turn by using only the handle bars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the curve.
questions.explanation: Always lean in the direction of the turn. Slow down before you enter the turn, not during it.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is usually most easily seen by other drivers when they are riding in which lane position?

options.text: The right
The center
The left

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: The center position is best for following a car because you will be visible in the driver's rearview mirror. Always be ready to change positions if needed.

questions.question: Before starting out, you should make sure the fuel valve is:

options.text: Open.
Closed.
Covered.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open.
questions.explanation: Open the fuel valve before you ride. If it is closed, the engine may start but will stall once the fuel in the lines runs out.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Move closer to the vehicle in front of you so you can use its lights to see farther down the road.
Keep riding at your normal speed to lower the risk of being struck from behind.
Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night and stay farther behind other vehicles. You cannot see as well in the dark, so you need more time and space to react to hazards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Yield to other drivers.
A stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.
Sit so your arms are straight when reaching for the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your elbows should bend slightly when holding the handlebars. Keep your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced.

questions.question: The key to making a quick turn is to:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Get your motorcycle to lean quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get your motorcycle to lean quickly.
questions.explanation: To make a quick turn, get your motorcycle to lean fast in the direction you want to go. The sharper the turn, the more the motorcycle must lean.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, you:

options.text: May exceed the speed limit by 10 mph.
Must not exceed the speed limit.
Are required to ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must not exceed the speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must stay within the speed limit when passing. Only pass when it is safe and legal.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have more time to react to the movements of other drivers.
You have space to maneuver.
You have limited escape route options.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have limited escape route options.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between you and other vehicles gives you more time to react and more room to maneuver safely.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should tell them to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible on the bike.
Avoid talking or moving unless necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking or moving unless necessary.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers not to talk or move while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should get on after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.

questions.question: If you get a flat tire while riding, you should:

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and stay off the brakes.
Shift your weight toward the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake on the good wheel while immediately pulling off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the handlebars tight and stay in a straight line. Only brake if you know which tire is flat. Slow down and exit the road safely.

questions.question: Part of your normal scanning routine while riding should include:

options.text: Constantly looking in the rearview mirror.
Checking the rearview mirror often.
Not using the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking the rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirror often as part of your normal scanning. Also use your mirror before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: When riding at night, keep a minimum following distance of:

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distances in the dark. Keep at least three seconds of space between you and the vehicle ahead when riding at night.

questions.question: Eye protection is:

options.text: Required for all riders.
Not required, but recommended.
Only required for inexperienced motorcycle users.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear eye protection on a moving motorcycle. A full face shield gives the best protection.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can:

options.text: Only be operated during the day.
Be operated without a driver license.
Be operated with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be operated with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, anyone with any class of driver license can operate a motorized scooter.

questions.question: When being passed by another vehicle, you should travel in:

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding near the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding far from it may cause the other driver to return to your lane too early.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists pass another vehicle?

options.text: In a staggered formation
In pairs
One at a time

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, motorcyclists should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing before the next one begins.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while you are stopping on a straightaway:

options.text: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You will need to release the rear brake to regain control of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks during a stop on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can usually control your motorcycle if it stays upright and moves straight ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming up ahead.
